verdict.line: You lose if you chip-poke Sett into Haymaker range and eat his banked Grit shield; you win if you dodge Facebreaker and let Feast stacks turn you into the bigger body by the mid-late game.

brief.thesis: Sett's W (Haymaker) banks every point of damage he takes as Grit and detonates it later as a shield plus a true-damage nova, so chip poke that doesn't threaten a kill just feeds his comeback tool. Cho'Gath has to win with discrete burst windows — Q (Rupture) into E (Vorpal Spikes) autos, timed for moments his E (Facebreaker) is down — rather than a constant poke war, and the matchup's real swing comes late once R (Feast) stacks make him the bigger body.

theirWindow.what: He can detonate W (Haymaker) for a shield and a true-damage nova at melee range, swinging the trade back his way — stop autoing and reset instead of continuing to poke.

yourWindow.what: Walk up and trade Q (Rupture) into E (Vorpal Spikes) autos — without Facebreaker he has no way to stun you mid-trade, so this is when you commit.

start.why: 46.9% win rate over 226 games at 70% pick — the mana sustain lets you spam Q (Rupture) poke through early trades instead of running dry against Sett's melee pressure.

boots.why: 48.7% win rate over 193 games at 61.5% pick — flattens the burst from Sett's empowered Q (Knuckle Down) punches, which otherwise scale off your max health.

core.why: Stacks max HP from ability casts, compounding with Feast's own HP growth so you out-scale Sett's flat kit rather than racing his early damage.
The burn and healing reduction undercut Pit Grit, the missing-health regen that otherwise keeps Sett alive through extended trades.
Punishes an auto-attack-reliant kit — Pit Grit's punches and Knuckle Down's empowered autos — with reflected damage; part of the 66.7% win-rate Heartsteel path.

situational.when: the enemy team has ranged poke beyond Sett and you need to close gaps to melee range
you're already ahead and want to snowball damage and sustain off Feast resets instead of pure tank stats
Sett's team stacks physical damage beyond just him and you need the extra armor and omnivamp

runes.keystoneWhy: The attack-speed burst on your first three attacks dumps Vorpal Spikes (E) procs instantly in a short trade window — land the burst before Sett's W (Haymaker) Grit shield comes online, then disengage.

summoners.why: Teleport is the most-played option (66.5% pick, 47.3% win rate) and lets you reset after the slower, window-based trade war this matchup calls for without losing side-wave pressure. Flash + Ignite (47.9% win rate, 27.7% pick) is the better call if you'd rather punish Sett's all-ins directly with Rupture into an Ignite execute.

playing.title: Don't feed his Haymaker
playing.detail: Every point of poke Sett takes is banked by W (Haymaker) as Grit and returned as a shield plus true-damage nova. Only commit poke when you can follow it into a real trade, not pure chip damage.

playing.title: Trade only off cooldown E
playing.detail: Sett's E (Facebreaker), 16 down to 10s at max rank, pulls enemies on opposite sides into a stun or a slow if you're on only one side. Stand on one side near minions so a whiff only slows you, and all-in right after he uses it.

playing.title: Respect empowered Q punches
playing.detail: Sett's Q (Knuckle Down), cooldown dropping from 9s to 5s with rank, makes his next two attacks deal bonus damage based on your max health and speeds him toward you. Back off the instant it triggers rather than eating both hits.

playing.title: Zone with Rupture, don't facetank
playing.detail: Use Q (Rupture), 9s cooldown and 950 range, to knock up and slow Sett before he closes distance. This keeps Vorpal Spikes (E) ticking on him from range instead of trading face to face where Pit Grit's regen favors him.

playing.title: Silence his engage with Feral Scream
playing.detail: W (Feral Scream), 13s cooldown, 300 range cone silence, shuts down Sett mid-cast on E (Facebreaker) or R (The Show Stopper). Hold it for that rather than spending it purely for poke damage.

playing.title: Stack Feast before scaling fights
playing.detail: R (Feast), 60s cooldown, deals true damage and grows your max health on a kill up to 6 stacks. Prioritize jungle camps and siege minions early so you're the bigger body once Heartsteel comes online.

playing.title: Don't poke him to a regen stalemate
playing.detail: Pit Grit heals Sett more as he drops low, so sustained chip damage alone won't finish him. Save Feast's true damage or a real all-in for the kill instead.

brief.patchCaveat: The build paths, rune pages, and summoner spell rates above are pulled from measured games on the current patch (16.20.1); the trade-pattern and timing reasoning is my own read of the kit, not something the win-rate data shows directly.

stats.opponentTip: Keep your distance from Sett’s (E) while poking from a distance. Do not let him activate his (P) by constantly dealing damge.
